forecaster_note: Decent sized to large surf but onshore and lumpy for most. There'll be plenty of mixed shorter to longer period S swell for head to overhead surf at most spots (S facing biggest as usual). It will be onshore and lumpy though with mostly poor conditions as winds trend from SE to E through the day. Although not completely blown out, if you don't mind putting up with the lump. Sheltered N-facing breaks and S corners will be cleaner in the morning but quite small — maybe getting a waist-high wave wrapping in. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: SSE onshore 16kph gusting 24, easing and swinging E through the afternoon — lumpy all day.

shark.summary: SharkSmart check pending this refresh — tap to check live detections

days.label: Today
days.note: Plenty of raw S energy — 451 kJ average, peaking 621 — but it's dead south at 168–178° and onshore SSE all day. Long Reef and Curl Curl are holding 4–8ft of lumpy closeout; Dee Why is getting the short end of the wrap at 3–5ft. A day to skip unless you just want a paddle.

dee-why.window: Not your day at Dee Why. If you go, 11am–1pm — Surfline nudges it to Fair midday and the SE eases to 15kph.
alerts: Swell is dead S (168–178°) — wraps badly into Dee Why, you're getting roughly half of Long Reef's size
SSE onshore 16kph gusting 24 all day, turning E — lumpy, no clean face

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: The Point needs some E in the swell to line up. At 168° it's a straight S — the bank won't wall, so expect short frontside runners off the corner rather than a proper right. Sit wide of the crowd on the shoulder.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 8am before the SE fills in. 621 kJ at 6am — the most energy on the coast today.
alerts: Biggest spot on the Northern Beaches today at 6–8ft — heavy, lumpy and consistent (100% at dawn)
Strong sweep with this much S energy — pick a rip line and stay on it

tip.label: Frontside off the point
tip.text: South-facing, so it eats this dead-S swell — that's why it's double Dee Why. Rights off the point run frontside for you, but at 6–8ft with 620 kJ behind it this is a paddle-fitness session, not a finesse one. Step up a board.

curl-curl.window: 6–8am at the south end for the cleanest of a lumpy lot. Fades fast after 9am.
alerts: 4–7ft and closing out on the bigger sets — south corner is the only workable bank
SSE onshore 17kph at dawn — already textured before you paddle out

tip.label: Both ways off the banks
tip.text: Curly's beachies take S swell better than Dee Why but they also close out on it. Work the south corner where the sand tapers — lefts will be the longer wave today, so backside. Shorter board, get under the lip early.

manly.window: Best bet mid-morning 9am–12pm. Smallest and most sheltered of the four — the fallback if the north is unrideable.
alerts: Sheltered from the raw S energy, so only 2–4ft while Long Reef is 6–8ft
Forecaster flags sheltered N-facing corners as cleaner but 'quite small'

tip.label: North Steyne banks
tip.text: The S corner near Queenscliff gets the cleanest wrap today. Small enough that you can actually surf it properly — grovel volume, and take the lefts backside off the bank rather than fighting the closeouts up the beach.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The good one. Winds swing NE with a light NNW at 9am, the S swell cleans up to head-high, and consistency hits 98%. Dee Why and Long Reef both go Fair — target 9am–12pm before the 22kph NE afternoon breeze.

dee-why.window: This is your session. 9am–12pm: NNW 5kph at 9am, glassy, swell cleaned up to 3–4ft+ with 100% consistency.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 10am. Still holding size off the point with light morning winds — best size-to-quality trade of the day.

curl-curl.window: 7–10am. Cleaner than today but still chunky; NE sea breeze builds to 22kph by 3pm.

manly.window: Mid-morning if you want small and easy. Least interesting of the four tomorrow.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Much smaller at 2–4ft and only 103 kJ, but a short-period NE swell finally replaces the dead S — the direction Dee Why and Long Reef actually want. Saturday has the light offshore morning and is the pick; Sunday goes onshore S and drops away.

dee-why.window: Saturday 8–11am. WNW/NW offshore but only 5kph — light and glassy rather than groomed. Sunday turns onshore S.

long-reef.window: Saturday morning. Short-period NE swell finally puts some E in the direction — the point actually lines up.

curl-curl.window: Saturday 8am–12pm. Peaky NE swell on the beachies with a light offshore — pick of the weekend.

manly.window: Saturday mid-morning. Small, clean and crowded.
